sections.text: My heart is oppressed with pity; and my mind confused as to what my duty is. Therefore, my Lord, tell me what is best for my spiritual welfare, for I am Thy disciple. Please direct me, I pray.
For should I attain the monarchy of the visible world, or over the invisible world, it would not drive away the anguish which is now paralysing my senses.
Sanjaya continued: Arjuna, the conqueror of all enemies, then told the Lord of All-Hearts that he would not fight, and became silent, O King!

So we had been discussing chapter two. We have seen in the first few verses that Arjuna continues to argue about why he feels that he should not be fighting. Obviously, we have spent the whole chapter one listening to his argument.
Then Bhagavan told him that why are you behaving this way? Where does this un Aryan like importance come upon you? In other words, this behavior which is not fitting to somebody who is civilized and trained about Dharma. As we have seen that in our culture everything is defined by Dharma. So whatever the basic qualities of the thing are being that defines who that person is.
So we have broadly a Manavadharma, what is the Dharma of a human being? We generally define the Dharma of a human being is to act according to his true self, which is Divinity, the expression of the God. So our Dharma as human being is to align our actions in line with the divinity. So everything we do should be keeping in mind that my true Dharma is divinity and therefore Im acting in that manner.
Then obviously we come down to now that I have aligned myself to divinity. Im now just playing a role in this life or in this state, or in this time. Now, whatever the role Im playing at that time will define what my Dharma is.
My Dharma from Monday through Friday is to act as an architect. So that time, what is right for me is defined by the role I have taken. On Sunday it will be different.
If I start talking about architecture here, it will be very inappropriate. So my Dharma changes as per the time and role I am taking. There is no universally I can say that if I behave this way will be appropriate.
I have to find what is the time I am in and what the role I have taken and then find what is my appropriate dharma. Arjuna right now is in a battlefield leading an army. Their army is depending on him on his strength and capability to win this war.
And now he wants to go back. Therefore Bhagavan said where the Un Aryan like behavior come upon you because as an Arya he was taught what is Dharma of a Kshatriya Kshatriya Dharma is when he is facing an enemy is to fight. Once he has decided this is the right battle, he has to fight.
So Bhagavanti, where does this behavior come from? Is it something that somebody was not clear enough while teaching you what a Dharmapakshatriya is? Or what is your Dharma as a prince? Or what is your Dharma as one of the Pandavas? Where is this behavior come from? So Arjuna obviously was not expecting that. He was expecting some sympathetic words. So he continues to make his point.
But then he realized that there may be something Im completely missing here, that all my arguments up till now has not made any impression on Krishna. So there may be something I need to think about what is right. And maybe Im not capable of thinking what is right.
So in the next few verses, Arjuna says: Karpanya Dosho Upahata Svabhavaha Pricchami Tvam. I made my argument thinking that what Im thinking is right, that this is my Dharma -- not to kill my teacher, not to kill my great grandfather, not to kill my cousins. For a while I thought, thats my Dharma. Now you are telling me that thats not my Dharma, that this is not Arya-like behavior.
Therefore Dharma Sammudha Chetah -- I am completely confused about what is Dharma right now. I do not know what my Dharma is. Pruchamitam, I am asking you, someone who is confused about his Dharma. What is my Dharma right now? What am I supposed to be doing at this time? Karpanya do so Aphatvah.
My own nature is overwhelmed by this pity, pity on me that I am facing the situation. I dont know what I am doing. Normally Im in my control.
Normally I know what Im supposed to be doing from my training, from my own intellect. I know in this situation how I should be behaving, which is most appropriate. But looks like my whole subhava.
My nature is overwhelmed by this pity about my own situation which Im facing. Therefore, I am Dharma Sammudhaha -- I am completely deluded about what is my Dharma. Is it not killing them is my Dharma.
Not fighting this war is my Dharma or fighting this war is my Dharma. Yat sreihaat nishitam bruhi tanme. Therefore you tell me with definitive guidance what is right for me.
Up till now he was using his own intellect and ego to come up with what is right and wrong. Then he put forward his argument. This is something, an indication to us that sometimes what we think through our intellect may not be right.
We do come up with all this argument about why Im doing this. You know, why I dont make any donation because they are all corrupt and all these organizations are corrupt. Why should I be supporting them? All this nice argument which I come up with, they may be just my own delusion.
As long as I hang on to my ego and my intellect to come up with the right answer. There may be right answer or there may be wrong answer. So right now, because you are telling me that what I was thinking is not right, Im assuming that Im completely deluded.
Now you tell me what is right for me. We go to ask advice, but typically we are not really ready to listen to the advice. We go to somebody and say, you know, this is what Im doing.
This is the situation. What do you think I should be doing? You know, the best thing for you to do is this. And you say, yeah, but I dont think Ill be able to.
Because then you can say, well, what does he know? I mean, obviously he doesnt know everything. We know what situation we are in. We are really asking for advice just to get confirmation of what Im thinking that somebody, yes, yes, you are right.
You shouldnt be doing that. I think what you did is very right. Thats what were really looking for.
We just need a little pat on our back saying, I think, Rajan, youre so smart. You figured out what to do. We are not really looking for advice.
Sisya Deham, I am your student. In our culture, Guru Sishya, relationship is very unique. It is very different from a father and a son or a mother and a son or a friend.
Shishya completely surrenders to the Guru once he finds that the Guru is appropriate. After that, there is no argument about what Guru says. Once he has surrendered to the Guru, then Guru tells him what to do and he does it.
It is not a relationship between a professor and a student. Students can argue here, there. Once I have decided thats my Guru, I have completely surrendered to him, and then whatever he says, without any argument, I will follow.
Because I have done all my homework before -- whether this should be my Guru, whether I should be learning this particular thing from him or not. Once that homework is done, I have completely surrendered. So he makes it clear to Krishna that Im not just simply asking advice from you because Im confused.
Im surrendering to you. Therefore, now you tell me what is Good for me and I will follow that. Sadhimam Tvam Prapannam I have taken refuge in you.
I have completely given up that I can come up with the right answer in this situation what is right and wrong. But I am now your student. You who will tell me what is right and wrong for me.
And whatever you tell me, I will do it now. One thing I learned many, many years ago -- and not from any of the teachers, but from Dr. Naidu, in whose house we used to do the classes.
He actually made me understand what surrender is. Surrender is something when you feel completely helpless. We go to temple and say I surrender to you Lord.
But we are really not. We really want to make sure that I am in control, who is behind me, who is ahead of me. They would be paying attention that I am putting donation.
So we are not really surrendering. Surrender is when I completely feel helpless. The example Dr.
Naidu gave me, which really stuck with me: two armies are fighting, and when does the one king decide hes going to surrender? When he feels completely helpless that there is no way hes going to win this battle, he surrenders to the other army. At that point hes completely helpless, completely at the mercy of the other king. The story of Porus and Alexander -- when Porus surrendered, Alexander asked him, How do you want me to treat you? And Porus said, Treat me like a king. Because at that point he has no other choice but to say I surrender.
Now you can treat me the way you want. But you asked me, so Im telling you, treat me like a king. So thats a surrender.
Surrender happens when you really feel that you dont have any other way out. And I surrender to you. Arjuna came to that point that my ego, my intellect, my all this training is of no value right now.
I cant come up with an answer which is going to be satisfactory to me or to you. Therefore Im now your student. Im asking you to teach me what is right and wrong.
Then tell me without giving options. If Krishna gives two options -- one, do this, and second, do that -- Im again confused. Dont give me options.
You know, when I came to this country, I must have told this story many, many times. But when I was in Africa to get a new car, you had to get in line, you had to register yourself. And then after two or three years you get notification from the dealership saying now your car has arrived and you can get it.
So to get a new car then everybody wants to get a new car. Everybody will come and congratulate you. Oh, thats a new car.
Oh, when did you register it? So my boss told me go and get a new car. So I come and tell everybody and they said, your boss is joking with you because by the time you get your new car you probably will be working someplace else. So I made all my effort to use all my influence to get a new car within six months.
And I was very proud. And as people have predicted, after eight months I was in the United States. I told my brother in law that it looks like there is no public transportation in this country.
He said no problem, well go over the weekend. Do you want to wait till weekend? He said, dont worry, well go over the weekend. Over the weekend he takes me first to a Chryslers dealership and there are cars till my eyes can see in the parking lot or that lot.
And he said, you can select any car, but let me tell you. And I said, you just tell me which car I should be buying. He said, this is just Chrysler.
Then we are going to go to gm, then well go to Ford and then if you like we can go to Toyota or other Japanese car. And I say Im getting dizzy, you just tell me which car I should be buying. Thats how Arjuna feels -- dont give me options, just tell me definitively what is right.

These verses mark a profound turning point: Arjuna admits My heart is oppressed with pity; my mind confused as to what my duty is and declares I am Thy disciple. Please direct me. This is the moment of true surrender - not when we pretend to give up control while secretly holding onto our opinions, but when we genuinely acknowledge that our own intellect has failed us. Arjuna recognizes that even ruling the monarchy of the visible world would not drive away his anguish.
True surrender, as taught here, happens when we feel completely helpless - like a defeated king who has no choice but to accept the mercy of his conqueror. We often go to others for advice while secretly wanting only validation of what we have already decided. Arjuna does something different: Tell me what is best for my spiritual welfare... without any options. He asks not for sympathy but for definitive guidance, committing in advance to follow whatever Krishna says.
Reflect today: When did you last truly surrender a decision to higher wisdom - whether to a teacher, to God, or to your own deeper conscience - without reserving the right to argue or reject the answer? What problem in your life might benefit from such complete surrender? Consider that the very act of admitting I dont know what to do with humility can be the doorway to genuine wisdom. Are you willing to be a true student, ready to follow guidance even if it contradicts your preferences?
